blocks.value: A constructor is a special method used to create and initialize an object. It's called using the new keyword: MyClass mc = new MyClass();

MyClass mc declares mc as a variable that will hold a MyClass object. MyClass() calls the constructor, which creates the object and returns its address, stored in mc. Notice a constructor has no return type at all — not even void.
A class can have multiple constructors, as long as their parameter lists differ — this lets you initialize an object in different ways depending on what information is available when it's created:
